title: Eliminate leaked strings in plugin provider adapter rebuilds
description:
## Finding

Provider adapter construction leaks heap strings to synthesize long-lived names. Reload/router rebuild cycles monotonically consume memory.

## Evidence at audited commit

`crates/thegn-host/src/plugin_providers.rs:29` and `crates/thegn-svc/src/plugin/provider.rs:143`.

## Implementation constraints

Use owned or shared immutable strings with lifetimes carried by the adapter/router. Do not replace leaks with dangling references or global mutable registries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No `Box::leak` or equivalent permanent allocation is used for dynamic plugin/provider names.
- [ ] Adapters own/share identity safely across router clones and asynchronous calls.
- [ ] Reload and provider-list churn release old generation allocations.
- [ ] Public traits use owned/Cow/Arc data where necessary without broad needless cloning.
- [ ] A stress test rebuilds routers thousands of times with stable retained memory.

## Verification

Run plugin provider unit/lifecycle tests plus leak-oriented stress instrumentation; run `just quick`.

## Execution dependencies

* **Blocked by:** THE-165
